title: Hof apply operation journal
description: /var/lib/hof/state/journal/<operationId>.json - the durable, per-apply-run header record on the target. Written once at apply start (immutable except `status`/`committedGeneration`, updated only by the same operationId that created it); individual operation attempts are recorded separately as an append-only operation-event-v1 log this journal's own operationId ties them to. Never holds a secret value, decrypted content, an environment dump, or an SSH private-key path - safe to read, copy, or attach to a bug report without a second sanitization pass.

approvedPlanId.description: The exact plan-v2 planId this run was approved against (--approve-plan-id) - equal to plan.planId below by construction (buildJournalDocument never accepts the two disagreeing).

plan.description: The full, exact plan-v2 document this operation was approved against - not just its planId. --resume reads operations[] directly from here rather than re-deriving a live baseline/diff (which is meaningless mid-bootstrap: managed resources the earlier, interrupted attempt already created would make a fresh resolveBaseline() see an already-applied host and wrongly refuse to resume at all - see PLATFORM-OPS-PLAN.md's "Item 8 reopened" entry). No schema in this repo cross-references another by $id (see this repo's own convention) - loosely typed here on purpose; the document was already validated against schemas/plan-v2.schema.json before ever being embedded (see plan-v2.mjs's own planV2Validator()).

inputDigests.description: Every input this specific run is bound to, fixed at journal creation and never recomputed from a live file again mid-run - a manifest/release-lock/catalog/renderer/Execution-Environment edited out from under an in-progress apply must never silently change what a resumed operation does.

status.description: in-progress: apply is running or was interrupted and not yet resolved either way. succeeded: every operation completed and state.commit landed - committedGeneration is then always set. failed: a fatal, unresumable outcome (see operation-event-v1's own resumability note) - the operator must diagnose and start a fresh bootstrap, never retry this same journal.

committedGeneration.description: Set only once state.commit has actually succeeded - null for the entire lifetime of a run that never reaches it, including every failed one. A bootstrap always commits generation 1.

allOf.description: The status/committedGeneration pairing this schema's own prose above already documents, actually enforced - a 2026-08-31 review found the invariant was prose-only, so a schema-valid but self-contradictory document (succeeded with committedGeneration still null; in-progress or failed with one already set) would have been silently accepted.
